title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The handwritten part continues the theorem from the previous page. That theorem describes the homomorphisms of simplicial differential rings A(S,S+,t)_* -> A'(S',S'+,t')_* between Grothendieck's divided-power (PD) de Rham objects. Here A_n = S{U_0..U_{n-1}}[dU_0..dU_{n-1}], with U_r = X_0+...+X_r. Such a homomorphism is given by a triple of data:
- phi_0 : S -> S', a ring map;
- A'_1 = sum_{j>=1} a'_j X_0^{(j)}, a PD series with no constant term;
- B'_i (i >= 1) in S'{X_0}.
The reconstruction formulas (next page) are phi(U_r^{(i)}) = A'^{(i)}{U_r} + B'_i{U_r} dU_r and phi(dU_r) = A'^{der}{U_r} dU_r, where A'^{der} = sum_j a'_j X_0^{(j-1)}.

Condition (3) comes from commutativity. Degree-0 source elements must have commuting images in the (graded-commutative) target. The cross terms give (A + B_i dU_r)(C dU_s) - (C dU_s)(A + B_i dU_r) = 2 B_i C dU_r dU_s, and similarly for two U-powers. So one needs 2 B'_i times the coefficients to vanish, i.e. 2 B'_i lies in the annihilator of the ideal J generated by the a'_j and b'_{jh}.

This page: (3) 'signifie que [2B'_i = 0 for all i >= 1]' as soon as J contains a regular element, in particular a unit. Two cases give such a unit:
- If phi is an isomorphism, the leading coefficient a'_1 of A'_1(X_0) = a'_1 X_0 + ... is invertible in S'.
- Under the hypotheses of 'cor. 5', suppose (phi_0(T))_pd = (T)_pd, i.e. phi_0(T) = sum lambda_i T^{(i)} with lambda_1 invertible. Then condition (2), sum a'_j t'^{(j)} = phi_0(t), gives a'_1 congruent to a unit modulo the PD ideal, so a'_1 is invertible.
In either case (3) can be rewritten as the boxed condition 2B'_i = 0 (i >= 1). This feeds the next page's corollaries: if 2 is invertible, B'_i = 0, so phi respects the gradings; and phi commutes with PD iff B'_i = A'^{(i-1)} B'_1.

The page was written on the back of an upside-down typescript, SGA 7 I, Exposé IX ('Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), p. 47, §4.6. That passage computes the length of Hom_{Z_l(Gamma)}(Sw, U(l)) via characters. It uses the filtration U^et ⊂ U^ef ⊂ U and the integrality and l-independence of the monodromy character (4.3 a)), giving the Swan conductor of an abelian variety as an integer independent of l. This is published material, reused as scrap paper.
errors: The precise necessary condition for commutativity is that 2·B'_i annihilates the coefficients of A'^{der} and of the B'_j (cross terms 2B_iC dU_r dU_s). It is not 2B'_i = 0 in general. The reduction to 2B'_i = 0 is valid only when a'_1 (or some regular element of J) is available, which is exactly what the page argues. The next page's phrase '2B'_i=0 (qui tient lieu de 3)' should be read under that hypothesis.

The step 'a'_1 ≡ 1 mod S'^+' requires matching phi_0(t) = sum a'_j t'^{(j)} with sum lambda_i t'^{(i)} and some freeness or uniqueness of PD expansions in t' (as in a PD polynomial or series situation, presumably the hypotheses of cor. 5). Literally one gets a'_1 ≡ lambda_1 (a unit) modulo the PD ideal, which suffices for invertibility.

ideas.what: Classification of morphisms of simplicial differential rings between PD de Rham simplicial objects by data (phi_0, A'_1, B'_i), with the obstruction 2B'_i = 0 arising from graded commutativity
ideas.modern_name: Endomorphisms/automorphisms of the PD de Rham complex of the PD affine line; non-graded (filtered) morphisms of de Rham-type dg algebras; relates loosely to G_a^# / PD-formal group structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (crystalline/PD de Rham theory: Berthelot, Illusie; stacky G_a^#: Drinfeld, Bhatt–Lurie)

ideas.what: Typescript on verso: l-independence and integrality of the Swan conductor of an abelian variety via the character of inertia on U(l)
ideas.modern_name: Swan conductor of abelian varieties, independence of l

deep.surprise_reason: Routine technical lemma (invertibility of the leading coefficient reduces the commutativity condition to 2B'_i = 0) in an unpublished computation on PD de Rham simplicial rings. The verso is published SGA 7 material.
transcription_corrections: '[ΣB'_i ≥ 0 ∀ i≥1]' should read '[2B'_i = 0 ∀ i ≥ 1]'; likewise the margin box is '2B'_i = 0 (i≥1)'.
'coefficient dominant a'_i de B'_1(X_0) = a'_1 X_0 + ...' should read 'coefficient dominant a'_1 de A'_1(X_0) = a'_1 X_0 + ...'.

'Il en est de même si φ est un isom (où φ est un isom)' is better read as: 'Il en est ainsi si φ est un isom (ou si ... un isom); en effet alors on voit que le coefficient dominant ... est inversible dans S''.
'(φ_0(T))_{p^d} = (T)_{p^d}' should read '(φ_0(T))_pd = (T)_pd' (PD ideals); 'λ_1 inversible' is written in the margin.
'a'_1 ≡ 1 mod S'^+_{K'}' is better read as 'a'_1 ≡ λ_1 (or 1) mod S'^+', with a'_1 'inversible' written in the margin, so that (3) becomes the condition 2B'_i = 0.
'Sw' in the typescript is the Swan module; 'a-Nδ+1' is consistent with SGA 7 IX.
